assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the system design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Do I need a special app?
faq.a: No. A notebook and a calendar are enough, and the course teaches how to keep tools simple.

faq.q: Is this for students or workers?
faq.a: Both. The examples use student and workplace situations.

faq.q: Does it replace mental health support?
faq.a: No. It gives practical habits, but if you feel overwhelmed for a long time, please talk to a doctor or counsellor.

activities.title: Audit one week of time
activities.objective: Total your hours by activity and see where time really goes.
activities.scenario: A student logged hours for a week. Work out totals and the share of the 168 hours of the week.
steps: In H2 total each activity across the days with SUM (fill down to H8).
In H9 total the hours logged.
In B11 find the unlogged time: 168 minus H9.
In I2 work out each activity's share of 168 hours: H2 divided by 168 (fill down).
Chart the totals as a bar chart.

checks.label: H2 totals sleep
checks.hint: =SUM(B2:G2)
checks.explain: Add the day columns for the row.

checks.label: H8 totals chores
checks.hint: Fill the formula down.

checks.label: H9 is the total logged
checks.hint: =SUM(H2:H8)

checks.label: B11 is the unlogged time
I2 is the share of the week
checks.explain: A share is part over whole.

checks.label: A bar chart of the totals
checks.hint: Chart type bar with labels A2:A8 and values H2:H8.
checks.explain: A picture shows the biggest uses of time.

activities.title: Plan a week
activities.objective: Write a weekly plan with three big priorities, time blocks and a buffer.
activities.scenario: A student has exams in two weeks, a project due Friday and wants to keep exercising. Plan the week.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'My week'.
Under Heading 2 'Top three priorities' write a numbered list of three.
Under Heading 2 'Time blocks' write a bulleted list of at least five blocks with day and time.
Under Heading 2 'Buffer and rest' say when you have slack time and when you rest.
Keep it between 100 and 260 words.

checks.label: A title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Three sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each.
checks.explain: Clear structure helps follow the plan.

checks.label: Three priorities
checks.hint: Use a numbered list of three items.

checks.label: At least five time blocks
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Time blocks turn intentions into appointments.

checks.label: Days and times appear
checks.hint: Mention days like Monday and times like 6 pm.
checks.explain: A block needs a day and a time.

checks.label: A buffer and rest are planned
checks.hint: Mention buffer, rest or a break.

checks.label: Between 100 and 260 words
checks.hint: A weekly plan on one page.

activities.title: Estimate with a buffer
activities.objective: Add a buffer to estimates so deadlines are realistic.
activities.scenario: A student estimates tasks for a project. Add a 30% buffer to each and see whether it fits in the hours available.
steps: In C2 enter the buffered hours: estimate times 1 plus the buffer in B8 (lock B8).
Fill down to C6.
In B7 total the buffered hours.
In B9 show Fits or Too much with IF, comparing B7 with the hours available in B10.

checks.label: C2 adds the buffer
checks.explain: Increase each estimate by the buffer.

checks.label: C6 is filled
checks.hint: Fill the formula down.

checks.label: C7 totals the buffered hours
checks.hint: =SUM(C2:C6)

checks.label: B9 says whether it fits
checks.hint: =IF(C7<=B10,"Fits","Too much")
checks.explain: Compare the total with the time you have.

activities.title: Track a habit
activities.objective: Count done days, work out a completion rate and find the longest gap.
activities.scenario: A student tracked a daily study habit for two weeks. Mark done days with 1 and missed days with 0.
steps: In B3 count the days done with SUM.
In B4 work out the completion rate: days done divided by days tracked (COUNT).
In B5 show Strong if the rate is at least 0.8, otherwise Build up, using IF.

checks.label: B3 counts the days done
checks.hint: =SUM(B6:B12)+SUM(D6:D12)

checks.label: B4 is the completion rate
checks.hint: =B3/COUNT(B6:B12,D6:D12)

checks.label: B5 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B4>=0.8,"Strong","Build up")
checks.explain: A threshold turns a number into a decision.

activities.title: Set a SMART goal and a first step
activities.objective: Write a goal that is specific, measurable and time-bound with a first action and a review date.
activities.scenario: You want to improve your English speaking before an interview in three months. Write the goal.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Goal'.
Write one sentence with a number and a date.
Add a Heading 2 'Weekly actions' with at least three bullets.
Add a Heading 2 'How I will measure it' with a short sentence.
Add a Heading 2 'Review' with a date and what I will do if I am behind.

checks.label: A goal title
checks.hint: Use Heading 1.

checks.label: Three more sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for Weekly actions, How I will measure it and Review.
checks.explain: A goal needs actions, measures and review.

checks.label: A number and a date
checks.hint: Include a number and a month or date.
checks.explain: A goal must be measurable and time-bound.

spec.what: a number and a time such as 3 months

checks.label: At least three actions
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Actions turn a goal into a plan.

checks.label: A review plan
checks.hint: Mention review and what to do if behind.

checks.label: Between 80 and 220 words
checks.hint: Concise.
